en: The Sūtra on Bathing the Image of the Buddha, translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Faju of the Western Jin Dynasty.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the devas and people of Mahāsthāna: "All of you, listen with one-pointed mind. The Buddha said:
He said:
"A human body is difficult to obtain, and so too is the Way of Non-action; a Buddha’s appearance in the world is likewise rare to encounter.

Since the time of incalculable kalpas past, I have been a layman, accumulating merit through successive eons. In every birth, I have disciplined myself, transmigrating through the five realms of existence, never coveting wealth or treasures, but casting away my own body in giving without any sense of attachment or regret."

Having attained the status of a prince, on the eighth day of the fourth month at midnight when the morning star appeared, he was born; upon falling to the ground, he took seven steps and, raising his right hand, spoke:
"In the heavens above and the world below, I alone am the most honored; I shall be the unsurpassed teacher for gods and humans."

When the Prince was born, the earth shook greatly; from the four Great Heavenly Kings up to the Brahma Heaven and the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the various devas therein each held twelve kinds of incense blended with warm water and various named flowers to bathe the Prince.
"The Prince shall attain the Way of the Buddha, manifesting the holy Dharma to deliver all sentient beings.
The Buddha addressed the devas and the people:

"The Buddhas of the ten directions are all born at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month; the Buddhas of the ten directions all leave the household life and enter the mountains to study the Way at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month."

The Buddhas of the ten directions all attain enlightenment at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month; the Buddhas of the ten directions all enter parinirvāṇa at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month.
The Buddha said:

"The reason the eighth day of the fourth month is used is that at the junction of spring and summer, calamities and transgressions have all come to an end; all things are flourishing everywhere while no toxic vapors have yet circulated. It is neither cold nor hot, and the seasonal climate is harmonious and appropriate—this is precisely the day the Buddha was born."

All you sons and daughters of good family, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, you should with a sincere mind recollect the Buddha and the power of his immeasurable merits; by bathing the images of the Buddha as if he were still present, you shall obtain immeasurable and incalculable merit.
The Buddha said:

"When I was originally practicing the bodhisattva path, thirty-six times I was Śakra, the King of Devas; thirty-six times I was a Wheel-Turning Sage King (Cakravartin); and thirty-six times I was a Universal Monarch (Vaiśravaṇa) who flies through the air."

All disciples of the Buddha who possess faith and virtuous intentions should mindfully contemplate the meritorious virtues of the Buddhas of the ten directions. If they bathe the images of the Buddhas with incense, flowers, and various offerings, all their aspirations shall be fulfilled; the devas, nāgas, and spirits will constantly follow and protect them, and all shall bear witness to this.
The Buddha told his disciples:

"Human existence is difficult to obtain, and the teachings of the sutras are difficult to hear. If there are devas or humans who can personally diminish their own share of wives and children or their wealth belonging to the five families to bathe the image of the Buddha, they shall obtain all their wishes just as when the Buddha was present in the world."

If you wish to seek deliverance from the world and attain the Way of Non-action (*asaṃskṛta*), so that birth does not meet with death, it can be attained; if you wish to seek diligent and courageous progress like that of Śākyamuni Buddha, it can be attained; if you wish to seek an *avaivartika* bodhisattva like Mañjuśrī, it can be attained; if you wish to seek a Wheel-Turning Sage King (*cakravartin*) who travels through the air to transform others, it can be attained; if you wish to seek the state of a Pratyekabuddha or an Arhat, it can be attained; if you wish to seek eternal departure from the three evil realms, it can be attained; if you wish to seek rebirth among gods and humans in wealth and joy, it can be attained; if you wish to seek a hundred sons and a thousand grandsons, it can be attained; if you wish to seek long life and freedom from illness, it can be attained.
The people of the world are as greedy as the ocean; they would rather cut a piece of flesh from their own bodies than give a single coin to another.

When one is born, one does not bring a single coin; when one dies, one does not take a single coin away. Wealth remains in the world while the person dies and must depart alone—reflecting on such suffering!
"Those who bathe the images of the Buddha carry this merit with them through birth and death, with no end in sight. The Buddha said,

"If a person possesses even a single thought of goodness and performs such meritorious deeds, all the celestial beings, benevolent spirits, the eight classes of devas and nāgas, and the Four Heavenly Kings will collectively protect and uphold them."

The merit and retribution arising from bathing the images of the Buddha ensure that one always attains purity; through these causes and conditions, one shall attain the Way of the Buddha. The following thirty-one lines of scripture are not present in the Danben (Dan-zang edition) but are found in the Songben (Song-zang edition); they are retained here.
The Buddha said:
“Those who take fine incense to bathe the image of the Buddha will themselves obtain blessings; their wisdom will abide in pure merit and renown.
Those who take fine flowers and scatter them over the Buddha will themselves obtain blessings; they will possess upright features and a beautiful complexion beyond compare.”
"Those who offer silk banners to the Buddha shall obtain blessings for themselves; wherever they are born, they shall naturally receive excellent and inexhaustible clothing.

The Buddha said, "I accumulated merit over successive lifetimes, practiced virtue with utmost sincerity, and through the observance of the precepts, patience, diligence, single-minded concentration, and wisdom, I have attained Buddhahood for myself."

Today, the virtuous one [Name], with a heart of universal loving-kindness and benevolent intent, having placed faith in the Buddha-way and desiring liberation, offers various incenses and flowers to bathe the image of the Buddha. This is for the sake of his parents of seven generations and five kinds of relatives, including brothers and wife, who are currently in distress; for the sake of those suffering diligently within the five realms of existence throughout the ten directions; and for the sake of the people of the Buddha’s realm who are ignorant and do not believe in the Buddha-way. May they, in future lives, be born as humans, handsome, pure, and white, respected by all, with no dust or grime adhering to their bodies.
Wherever they are born, they will always encounter the Buddha;
wherever they are born, they will always encounter the Dharma;
wherever they are born, they will always encounter the community of bhikṣus.

May such-and-such a person master the scriptures and possess clear wisdom regarding the Buddha’s twelve divisions of the canon, the four Āgamas, the *ānāpāna-smṛti*, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, and the eightfold noble path; if they can seek the Way of the Buddha with a sincere heart, they shall swiftly attain the stage of *avaivartika*.
"May they attain the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics of a Buddha, with a complexion like purple-polished gold;
as well as the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique qualities."
From his mouth shall issue eight kinds of sounds; he shall fly through the air and possess penetrating vision, reaching wherever he goes.
Devas, nāgas, spirits, and the retinues of the Mother of Ghosts (Hārītī) shall protect his person, ensuring that his coming and going are always peaceful and secure.

If one travels through mountains, may one not encounter tigers or wolves; if one enters military ranks, may one not be struck by weapons; if one travels upon rivers or lakes, may one not encounter wind or waves.

May there be no one on one's bed afflicted by illness or emaciation; may there be no summons from local officials; and for those with wives or daughters facing the difficulty of childbirth, may they attain peace and security.

If one engages in trade and commerce, their profits shall increase a hundredfold; various malevolent influences shall not dare to interfere, and fire, water, thieves, robbers, enemies, or creditors shall not dare to cause them harm.

"May their speech be extinguished and they all be brought to subjection; may they be made to practice with diligence so that they do not fall into mid-course regret, acting like Bodhisattvas and attaining the Way like Buddhas.

This *Sūtra on Washing Buddha Images*—which in the Song Canon is titled the *Mahācchattra Sūtra* translated by Śīladharma—is now revised according to the *Kaiyuan Lu*, as the Song Canon contains errors. Thus, following the Danben (Northern) edition, it is changed to the *Sūtra on Washing Buddha Images* translated by Dharmaprabha.

Furthermore, at the very beginning of this scripture in the Song edition, it states: "Mahāsthāna, etc., up to two pages of scriptural text. This is entirely the text of the *Mahāsthānaprāpta-sūtra*; the two scriptures are not different.

Now, following the Dan edition, the two pages beginning with "At that time the Buddha addressed Mahākātyāyana" and ending with "by these causes and conditions one attains the Buddha-way" have been separated.
The thirty-one lines of scripture following "Having bathed the Buddha’s image at the Buddha’s command" were originally present in the Song edition itself, and they still exist there today.
